dinner leftovers for lunch—meat, rice, cheese, fruit, and so
on. For dietitians, food is our profession; but for patients
newly diagnosed with celiac disease, we forget that they
now have to think about every bite they take, and it’s over-
whelming. I try to hook them up with a support group, so
they can network with others, and it helps them cope with
the diet and the disease.

have to convince doctors to not tell patients to try the diet
before they have the diagnostic serological tests and biopsy
as these tests may come back negative if the patient is
avoiding gluten.
When I started out, I wasn’t an expert in celiac disease,
but I had clients who needed help, so I did my homework.
